era: Arcade / Master System / Genesis / Game Gear / Saturn / PlayStation 2 / Nintendo 3DS / modern platforms
summary: Sega's ninja action series starring Joe Musashi and successors, spanning arcade originals, Genesis classics, handheld spin-offs, 3D PS2 entries, and Shinobi: Art of Vengeance.

entries.title: Shinobi

emulation.emulator: Sega Ages / MAME / Master System emulator for supplement
emulation.notes: Use the official Sega Ages release for the main playthrough; MAME is the preservation fallback.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade emulation with Switch Sega Ages options

primary.why: The original Shinobi is an arcade System 16 game with many ports. The Switch Sega Ages release is the modern official arcade-version route, while the Master System version is worth a secondary look for its altered health/hostage/bonus-stage systems.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Sega Ages arcade release on Switch; sample the Master System port separately if you want its different mechanics.

secondary.exclusive_content: Altered health gauge, optional hostage rescues, different upgrade/bonus-stage structure, and required hostage rules
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Master System port after the arcade version if you want the distinct 8-bit conversion design.
secondary.why: It is not the highest-fidelity route, but it is mechanically different enough to preserve as a supplement.

entries.remaster_caveats: Older Wii/Xbox 360 arcade releases had graphical licensing modifications; Switch Sega Ages is the preferred modern route.

emulation.notes: Use arcade hardware or accurate emulation.

primary.why: Shadow Dancer is the arcade sequel to Shinobi and runs on Sega System 18 hardware. The Genesis game is a separate loose adaptation, so the arcade original remains the primary for this entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play an original cabinet or a legal arcade-emulation setup; use the Genesis Secret of Shinobi entry separately for its distinct content.

entries.title: The Revenge of Shinobi

emulation.notes: Use a modern official ROM/reissue or accurate Genesis emulation.

primary.version: Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern collection or emulator
primary.why: The Revenge of Shinobi is a Genesis/Mega Drive game with many later collection/digital routes. Because older revisions contained culturally recognizable enemy likenesses that were revised for rights reasons, a modern official Genesis/Mega Drive release is the cleanest archival route.
primary.how_to_play: Play via Sega Genesis Classics, Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack, original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, or BlastEm.

entries.remaster_caveats: Multiple revisions exist because of character-likeness/copyright issues; no full remake is known to exist.

emulation.notes: Use Master System emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: Alex Kidd in Shinobi World is both an Alex Kidd game and a Shinobi spoof, developed from the Shinobi Kid prototype. The Master System release is the content baseline, while Wii Virtual Console was only an older reissue route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Master System version on original hardware or a Master System emulator; use Wii Virtual Console only if already owned.

entries.title: Shadow Dancer: The Secret of Shinobi

emulation.notes: Use an accurate Genesis/Mega Drive route or modern collection.

primary.version: Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern collection or emulator
primary.why: The Secret of Shinobi is a loose Genesis/Mega Drive adaptation of arcade Shadow Dancer with different levels, character art, dog mechanics, and hostage objectives. The Genesis/Mega Drive version is the full game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version via original hardware, Sega Genesis Classics, Steam, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, or BlastEm.

emulation.notes: Use Master System emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: The Cyber Shinobi is a Master System-exclusive futuristic sequel, released in Canada, Europe, Australia, and Brazil after the system had ended in other markets. No alternate release route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Master System cartridge on original hardware or a Master System emulator.

emulation.notes: Use Game Gear emulation, original hardware, or owned 3DS Virtual Console copy.

primary.why: The G.G. Shinobi was the first Shinobi made specifically for a portable platform and uses a character-switching rescue structure. The later 3DS Virtual Console release is an access route to the same Game Gear title.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Gear version on original hardware, Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console where owned, or a Game Gear emulator.

entries.title: The G.G. Shinobi II: The Silent Fury

emulation.notes: Use Game Gear emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: The Silent Fury is a Game Gear-exclusive sequel built around rescuing allied ninjas and retrieving elemental crystals. No alternate platform route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Gear cartridge on original hardware or a Game Gear emulator.

entries.title: Shinobi III: Return of the Ninja Master

emulation.notes: Use an accurate Genesis/Mega Drive route or modern official collection.

primary.version: Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern collection or emulator
primary.why: Shinobi III is a Genesis/Mega Drive sequel that later appeared on many compilations and digital services. The final 1993 Genesis/Mega Drive game is the definitive content; the leaked earlier beta is not an official release.
primary.how_to_play: Play via Sega Genesis Classics, Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack, original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, or BlastEm.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remake/remaster exists; many modern routes are emulated collection releases.

entries.title: Shinobi Legions
entries.definitive_edition: Japanese/North American Saturn release plus European soundtrack supplement

emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation or original hardware; choose region based on soundtrack preference.

primary.why: Shinobi Legions is a Saturn-only entry. The European Shinobi X release changes the in-game soundtrack, while the Japanese/North American releases keep the original score, making them the main archival route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese or North American Saturn release on original hardware or a Saturn emulator; sample the European Shinobi X version only for its alternate Richard Jacques score.

secondary.what_to_play: Sample the European release if you want the alternate soundtrack.
secondary.why: The gameplay is otherwise the same Saturn-only game, but the music is region-specific.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high-resolution PS2 play or PS3 PS2 Classic where owned.

primary.version: Original PS2 release via PS2 Classic where owned
primary.why: The 2002 Shinobi reboot was released for PS2 and later as an emulated PS2 Classic on PS3. It includes unlockable Joe Musashi and Moritsune/Aomizuchi content after progress conditions, so the original PS2 build is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS2, PS3 PS2 Classics where owned, or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscale.

emulation.notes: Use GBA emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: The 2002 Game Boy Advance game shares the title and ninja-action premise with the 1989 Genesis game, but it is not a continuation or port of that game. It is a separate handheld entry with only one known release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GBA cartridge on original hardware or mGBA; do not treat it as a version of the 1989 Genesis game.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high-resolution PS2 play.

primary.why: Nightshade, known as Kunoichi in Japan, is a PS2-only sequel to the 2002 Shinobi with Hibana as lead and unlockable Hotsuma/Joe routes tied to save/mission conditions. No alternate platform release is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscale.

emulation.notes: Original 3DS hardware best preserves stereoscopic presentation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original 3DS stereoscopic output or emulator upscale

primary.why: Shinobi 3D was developed for Nintendo 3DS, released worldwide in November 2011, and has no alternate release documented. Its stereoscopic 3D presentation and touchscreen minigames tie it to the 3DS hardware.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 3DS cartridge on original 3DS hardware; use Citra/Lime3DS-style emulation only if compatibility and dual-screen layout meet your needs.

entries.title: Shinobi: Art of Vengeance

primary.why: Art of Vengeance is Lizardcube's 2025 hand-drawn revival, released for Switch, PlayStation, Xbox, and Windows. Windows is the highest-fidelity/configurable route, while PS5 was the reviewed console route in public review coverage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version for fidelity/configuration; choose PS5 or Xbox Series X/S if you prefer fixed console performance.

entries.remaster_caveats: New revival rather than remake of a specific older Shinobi entry.
